By this application under section 483(3) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the applicant-State has prayed for the following reliefs;
"(A) Your Lordship may be pleased to admit and allow this application.

(B) Your Lordship may be pleased to quash and set aside the order dated 01.11.2021 passed in Criminal Misc. Application No.138 of 2021 passed by the Learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Dhari and thereby cancel regular bail granted by the Learned Additional Sessions Judge.

2. Facts in brief leading to the filing of the present NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined application are that the complainant, namely, A.P. Dodiya,
P.S.I., Chalal Police Station had filed a complaint at Chalala Police Station, Amreli vide Part (B) C.R.
No.11193013210422 of 2021 on 19.07.2021 for the offence punishable under Section 20(B) and 29 of the NDPS Act.

As per the case of the complainant, the huge quantity of Ganja worth Rs.64,000/-
were found from the conscious possession of the respondent- accused.
The total weight of the contraband substance was 6.4 kg.
2.3 After the registration of the FIR, the respondent-accused came to be arrested and sent to the judicial custody.

2.4 Therefore, the respondent preferred regular bail application before the Sessions Court at Dhari being Criminal Misc. Application No.138 of 2021, which was strongly opposed by the investigating officer by filing an affidavit dated 01.11.2021.

2.5 Thereafter, vide the impugned order dated 01.11.2021, the respondent-accused was enlarged on regular bail by the Additional Sessions Judge, Rajula, being aggrieved with which, the State is here before this Court with the present application, seeking cancellation of bail.

3. Learned APP Mr. Soni appearing for the applicant submitted that the bail granted to the respondent-accused deserves to be cancelled being illegal, improper, arbitrary and against the provisions of law.

He submitted that the Sessions Judge ought to have considered the fact that the respondent is the owner of the place from where contraband substance 'Ganja' worth Rs.64,000/-
was recovered.
The respondent - NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025
undefined accused was having the conscious possession and knowledge of the drugs.

Learned APP further submitted that the learned Sessions Judge ought to have considered the fact that the raid had been carried out as per the mandatory provisions of NDPS Act and in the presence of the Panchas.
Moreover, the learned Sessions Judge also ought to have considered that there are five past antecedents against the respondent-accused.
He also submitted that the respondent-accused is a habitual offender and known for the illegal activities in the Chalala area.

Learned APP further submitted that the respondent-accused is a habitual offender, and therefore, well acquainted with the tactics that how to escape from the clutches of law, and therefore, he used to adopt a modus of trading in less than commercial quantity of drugs.
He submitted that the impugned order of bail is almost like a judgment of acquittal ignoring relevant aspects and principles as regards grant of bail in an offence under the NDPS Act.
Thus, it has been submitted that the bail granted in favour of the respondent-accused deserves to be cancelled.

4. On the other hand, the present application has been vehemently opposed by learned advocate Mr.
Chaudhary appearing for the respondent-accused.

He submitted that as per the case of the State Of Gujarat vs Ramkubhai Danabhai Vala on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63928406/
2 prosecution, the contraband substance was recovered from the house of the respondent-accused,
however, there is no ownership proof being placed on record along with the charge-sheet papers which indicates that the respondent-accused is the owner of the house.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, the respondent-accused is an agriculturist and there is no any past antecedents against him under NDPS Act.

Learned advocate NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED:
06/08/2025 undefined Mr. Chaudhary further submitted that the contraband Ganja was of the intermediate quantity, and as such, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly exercised its discretion in favour of the respondent-accused.

Moreover, the respondent-accused has been released on bail after filing of the charge-sheet, and now almost more than three and half yers have been passed since the grant of bail, and there is not a single instance being brought to the notice of the Court that the respondent-accused has committed breach of any of the conditions imposed by the trial court while releasing him on bail.

Moreover, charge has already been framed and, summonses have also been issued to the witnesses, and as such, at this stage, after a period of more than three and half years,
and when there is substantial progress in the trial, the impugned order dated 01.11.2021 is not required to be interfered with, and thus, the present application deserves to be rejected.

5. Heard the learned APP and the learned advocate appearing for the respondent-accused, as also perused the record.
6.

The case on hand pertains to cancellation of bail granted to the accused, and according to me, in an application for cancellation of bail, the conduct subsequent to release on bail and the supervening circumstances are the relevant factors to be kept in mind while deciding the cancellation of bail application.

It is no doubt true that the error being committed by the learned trial judge as well as the non-consideration of relevant aspects while setting the accused at liberty are also the relevant factors to be borne in mind at the time of deciding NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined cancellation of bail application, still the same do not have much significance, on the basis of which, the order granting bail to the accused can be reversed, as it may be taken into consideration and determined during the course of trial.

The consideration of cancellation of bail is different from the consideration for grant of bail, and the bail can be cancelled only on existence of cogent and overwhelming circumstances, but not on re- appreciation of the facts of the case.
It is a settled law that cancellation of bail should not be by way of punishment even if prima facie case against the accused is established.

7. I have also gone through the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge, and it appears from the same that all the relevant aspects germane to the grant of bail have been considered by the Sessions Judge and, therefore, the discretion exercised could not be said to be perverse or illegal in any manner.
8. I have also gone through the averments made in the application.

It appears from the same that,
the cancellation is sought for on the ground that some relevant aspects were not taken into consideration by the learned trial judge while enlarging the accused on bail.
Here, in the case at hand, it is not the case of the complainant that the respondents-accused has breached any of the conditions imposed upon him by the trial court while being released on bail.

The respondent- accused is at liberty since 01.11.2021, i.e. for more than three and half years, and during this period,

sentences.text: not a single incident of non-compliance of the order passed by the trial court is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined reported against the respondent-accused, or brought on record before this Court.

Hence, solely on the ground that some relevant aspects were claimed to have been not taken into consideration by the trial court, the entire order of granting bail to the respondents-accused cannot be vitiated.

9. Moreover, while considering degree of burden of prove lie upon prosecution or complainant/Informant, when an application for cancellation of bail moved, is not to the extent of proving by a mathematical certainty or beyond reasonable doubt but it must establish its case by showing on a preponderance of probabilities that accused has attempted or may attempt to or tamper or has tampered with witnesses.
It may also be proved by test of balance of probabilities that accused has abused his liberty or it may show that there is reasonable apprehension that he will interfere with course of justice.

This Court approved Bombay High Court decision in Madhukar Purshottam Jondkar vs. Talab Haji Hussain 60 Bombay Law Reporter 465 that test adopted by the Court would be, whether material placed before it is such as to lead to the conclusion that there is a strong prima facie case that accused if allowed to be at large he would tamper with prosecution witnesses and impede course of justice.

entities.text: Madhukar Purshottam Jondkar vs. Talab Haji Hussain 60 Bombay Law Reporter 465
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mere unfounded apprehension or self imagined threat by prosecution or Informant-Complainant would not justify cancellation of bail, granted to accused.

10. In Raghubir Singh vs. State of Bihar (1986) 4 SCC 481, the Court held that grounds for cancellation of bail under Sections 437(5) and 439(2) are identical, namely, bail granted under NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined Section 437(1) or (2) or Section 439(1) can be cancelled where (i) accused misuses his liberty by indulging in similar criminal activity, (ii) interferes with the course of investigation, (iii) attempts to tamper with evidence or witnesses, (iv) threatens witnesses or indulges in similar activities which would hamper smooth investigation, (v) there is likelihood of his fleeing to another country, (vi) attempts to make himself scarce by going underground or becoming unavailable to the investigating agency, (vii) attempts to place himself beyond the reach of his surety, etc.
11.

entities.text: Raghubir Singh vs. State of Bihar (1986) 4 SCC 481
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also held that above grounds are illustrative and not exhaustive.
Rejection of bail stands on one footing but cancellation of bail is a harsh order since it interferes with liberty of individual and must not be lightly resorted to.

12 In Dolat Ram and others vs. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349, the Court held that rejection of bail in a non-bailable case at initial stage and cancellation of bail so granted, has to be dealt with and considered on different basis.

entities.text: Dolat Ram and others vs. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing cancellation of bail, already granted.

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Ramkubhai Danabhai Vala on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Court also reminded that bail once granted should not be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying concession of bail during trial.

14. In CBI, Hyderabad vs. Subramani Gopalakrishnan and others (2011) 5 SCC 296, in para 23,
Court said :
"....that there is difference between yardstick for cancellation of bail and appeal against the order granting bail.

entities.text: CBI, Hyderabad vs. Subramani Gopalakrishnan and others (2011) 5 SCC 296
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the cancellation of bail already granted.

Generally speaking, the grounds for cancellation of bail are, interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of justice or evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concessions granted to the accused in any manner.
These are all only few illustrative materials.
The satisfaction of the Court on the basis of the materials placed on record of the possibility of the accused absconding is another reason justifying the cancellation of bail.

In other words, bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial."

15. Position, influence and resources of accused have also been held relevant factors to adjudge whether accused is likely to interfere with administration of justice, trial or tamper with witness or evidence.

16. Considerations and relevant aspects by a Court while granting a bail are different than those when an application for cancellation of bail has come up before the Court and this NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined aspect has been considered by a three-Judges Bench of Supreme Court in State (Delhi Administration) vs. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411 wherein the Bench had an occasion to consider an order dated 11.04.1978 passed by Delhi High Court rejecting Delhi Administration's application for cancellation of bail of respondent Sanjay Gandhi.

entities.text: State (Delhi Administration) vs. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court observed that rejection of bail, when bail applied is one thing;
cancellation of bail already granted is quite another.
It is easier to reject a bail application in a non-bailable case than to cancel a bail granted in such a case.

Cancellation of bail necessarily involves review of a decision already made and can, by and large, be permitted only, if, by reason of supervening circumstances, it would be no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow accused to retain his freedom during the trial.
17.
In X vs. The State of Telangana and Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5 anticipatory bail from Sessions Judge on 13.01.2017 and had advantage of that order for about eight months.
The said order was cancelled by Sessions Judge on the ground that accused has not disclosed that he was also accused in 2G Spectrum case.
This cancellation order was affirmed by High Court and also by Supreme Court.
Thereafter accused moved a bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C., which was allowed by High Court and accused was released on bail.
This order was challenged in appeal before Supreme Court.
Upholding the said order, Court said that bail once granted should not be cancelled unless a cogent case, based on supervening event has been made out.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7465/2022 ORDER DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined 18.
In Seema Singh vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors.

entities.text: Seema Singh vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2018) 16 SCC 10 bail granted to accused by High Court in the case registered under Sections 498-A, 302, 120-B IPC was challenged in appeal before Supreme Court.
The Court noticed that accused-2's bail application was rejected by Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ghaziabad and thereafter bail was granted by High Court.
The Court said that gravity of offence is a relevant factor but not the sole ground to deny bail if there are other overwhelming circumstances justifying grant of bail.
Noticing special feature, Court upheld order of High Court granting bail.

19. Thus, the broad principles, which are to be considered by this Court while granting bail and when bail is already granted but an application for cancellation has come up for consideration, as discussed above, show that there is no thumb rule in both the situations.
However, it is true that factors relevant for grant of bail are different and approach required to be adopted while considering application for cancellation of bail is different.

20. Looking to above exposition of law as also the fact and circumstances of the case, I find that there is no material available on record to show any justification for cancellation of bail after more than three and half years and, therefore, order of cancellation of bail cannot be justified at this stage.
21.
In the result, the present application fails and is hereby rejected.
(DIVYESH A. JOSHI,J) VAHID State Of Gujarat vs Ramkubhai Danabhai Vala on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63928406/
